correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\), all baseline masses and normalized quadratic weights are positive. The bounded-support identity \(\operatorname{Var}(Y)=m(n-m)-\mathbb E[Y(n-Y)]\) gives the strict \(0<R_n<n\) bound. With fixed \(q\ne0\), factorial-moment estimates produce \(p_0=2/(2+q^2)+2q\sqrt{n\alpha}/((2+q^2)\sqrt\beta)+O(\beta^{-1})\), the opposite first-order \(p_1\) deviation and higher masses \(O(\beta^{-1})\), proving the sharp TV rate and Bernoulli limit. A diagonal choice \(q_j=j\), then sufficiently large finite \(\beta_j\), approaches the lower endpoint; the unweighted symmetric small-shape limit approaches the upper. Continuity on a path-connected domain fills every interior ratio. The \(n=2\) rational witness and 428 finite checker groups support but do not replace these arguments.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary paper supplies the weighted pmf, moments and coefficient-of-variation plots, not the exact full equimean-binomial variance ratio image or the \(n\ge2\) Bernoulli rare-count limit with sharp total variation coefficient. The 2020 shifted-Poisson weighted model uses a different baseline and benchmark; the 2022 discretized-beta-mixture model has a different mixing mechanism. Related finite beta-binomial papers address ordinary BB log-concavity, thinning, and separate bi-uniform mixture dispersivity, which neither subsume nor imply these sharp BBB results. Query results and material read give best-knowledge priority only.

value.rationale: The exact binomial-variance comparison is central to selecting a bounded count model when the source was proposed for overdispersion: the same family spans every attainable relative variance from almost \(0\) to almost \(n\). The model-specific Bernoulli transition and explicit sharp TV rate explain a strong, mathematically nontrivial underdispersion mechanism at every fixed nonzero tilt. This is an exhaustive natural phase range, not an ad hoc numerical increment.
